qs.q: What is the primary mechanism responsible for normochromic normocytic anemia in chronic kidney failure?
o: Severe vitamin B12 and folate malabsorption
Primary bone marrow failure from uremic toxins
qs.e: Normochromic normocytic anemia principally develops from decreased renal synthesis of erythropoietin and becomes more severe as the GFR progressively decreases. There is no reticulocyte response, and RBC survival is also decreased.

qs.q: A 51-year-old woman with chronic kidney failure on hemodialysis presents with painful, violaceous skin ulcers on her abdomen and thighs. Biopsy demonstrates media calcification of small arterioles and microthrombi. Which laboratory abnormality is most closely associated with this syndrome?
qs.e: Skin necrosis in calciphylaxis is strongly associated with a poorly controlled calcium-phosphate product leading to systemic vascular calcification. While anemia and erythropoietin resistance are common in kidney failure, they do not directly drive medial arteriolar calcification.
